tts: Why is everyone suddenly a fitness influencer? And do they really all make good money? Spoiler: the money isn't coming from views.

Fitness is perfect content. A new workout every day, new meals, and a visible result: before and after. Then the pandemic closed the gyms, and millions of people started working out at home, from videos.
But views pay pennies. So the first step is sponsorships and promo codes: an influencer recommends a protein powder or leggings and gets a cut of every sale.
Step two: their own programs and online coaching. A workout is filmed once, but sold thousands of times, at almost no extra cost.
Step three: their own brand. Fitness influencer Katy Hearn started an energy drink and supplement brand, and in twenty twenty-five it sold for one point eight billion dollars.
And trainer Kayla Itsines sold her workout app for hundreds of millions, then later bought it back for far less.
But here's the catch: they're the exception. By some estimates, only about four percent of creators make over a hundred thousand dollars a year. Most earn very little. You just don't see them.
So a successful fitness influencer isn't really selling workouts. They're selling trust, and then turning it into a product of their own.
